html:
The Thai script was, by tradition, created in 1283 by King Ramkhamhaeng of Sukhothai. It was adapted from the Old Khmer script, itself from Indian writing.

Its earliest known text is the Ramkhamhaeng inscription, which describes a prosperous Sukhothai with free trade and a bell that people could ring to call the king. Some scholars have questioned when the stone was really carved, but most accept it.

Unlike Khmer, the Thai alphabet marks tones, needed for the Thai language. With changes, it has been used ever since, and the Lao script is a close relative. It is a pillar of Thai identity. See Sukhothai and Ayutthaya.
